dyslexicsteak opened PR #15025 from dyslexicsteak:compose-in-memory to bytecodealliance:main:

Compose the main Wasm and its compile-time builtins directly with wasm_compose::graph::CompositionGraph instead of writing them to a temporary directory and running the file-based ComponentComposer. Only builtins registered on the CodeBuilder can be composed in.

This also skips composition when the main Wasm imports no builtin, and drops the tempfile dependency of the compile-time-builtins feature.

This resolves a security issue and fixes various filesystem path related bugs and also adds tests with more realistic name inputs.

Fixes #15024.

:memo: fitzgen submitted PR review:

Thanks! Overall looks good, but a few things we should address before merging below.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

This comment seems like it belongs on top of let label = ... below, rather than here.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

This seems unnecessary?

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

I think this means that we will define and instantiate every builtin, even if it isn't used, which I believe would be a regression from our current behavior, and matters since it might make a component grow past the configured limits for number of memories or whatnot in the pooling allocator, for example.

Instead, we should figure out which builtins are needed by the program, and then only include and instantiate those.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

I don't think we want to enable all features here. Instead, we want to get the feature set from the wasmtime::Config, which is accessible from the wasmtime::Engine and so should also be accessible from a CodeBuilder: https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/blob/48c6579c9a1eaee45a5062b2e07ab3b5a69bae9b/crates/wasmtime/src/config.rs#L2585

dyslexicsteak commented on PR #15025:

Thanks! Overall looks good, but a few things we should address before merging below.

The feedback has got me thinking, actually, and maybe this requires an issue to discuss and a 2nd PR, but what if builtins resolved transitively? Like, say an embedder splits builtins into layers that build upon each other, with "ns:host/buffers" and "ns:host/strings" building on "ns:host/memory", as it stands right now, if a guest uses the higher-level builtins on their own then the lower level "ns:host/memory" won't get composed in because it's not a direct guest import. If they resolved transitively then it just works for any import anywhere and works fine based on my local testing.
:memo: fitzgen submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: fitzgen created PR review comment:

D'oh I missed that this was already looping over the main component's imports.
